title: Silverpine - Assurance Form Walkthrough with Redwood
customer_attendees: Dana Ortiz - Head of IT Risk
summary: Intro + walkthrough of customer's vendor assurance questionnaire (SIG-derived) focusing on SOC2/ISO controls, SSO/RBAC, KMS evidence, audit logs retention and EU data residency. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share SOC2 report, ISO scoping note, KMS architecture diagram, sample audit-log export, and a checklist mapping to Silverpine's assurance form. Follow-up deep-dive with security team scheduled.
topics: Data residency and private deployment options
action_items: Maria Chen - Send SOC 2 Type II report and scoping note for ISO 27001 - Due: 2026-08-07
Omar Ruiz - Prepare KMS/HSM network diagram and sample KMS policies - Due: 2026-08-10
Maria Chen - Share evidence checklist mapping to Silverpine SIG questions (spreadsheet link) - Due: 2026-08-06
Kyle/Priya/Maria - Schedule security deep-dive for Aug 13 - Due: 2026-08-05
next_steps: Redwood to email SOC2 report and a short ISO scope note
Redwood to attach KMS/HSM diagram and sample audit logs (anonymized)
Customer to confirm any additional residency constraints for EU/UK
Schedule follow-up technical deep-dive for 60–90 minutes with Security+Infra teams
transcript:
[00:00] Maria Chen: Hi everyone thanks for making time today. I'm Maria from Redwood, AE on the account. Omar from our SE team is here too.
[00:06] Dana Ortiz: Hey Maria, hi Omar. Thanks, we'll try to be concise—Priya and Kyle are on.
[00:11] Omar Ruiz: Great, quick agenda, we'll walk the Silverpine assurance form you sent, call out where we can provide evidence (SOC2/ISO), and cover KMS/SSO and logging detail.
[00:21] Priya Anand: Sounds good. Procurement angle — timeline is tight, we need to close vendor screening within three weeks.
[00:26] Maria Chen: Understood. We'll prioritize SOC2 artifacts and a SIG mapping spreadsheet so you can see direct answers.
[00:31] Kyle Mercer: Quick thing up front: we run Splunk for logs, need to understand retention, schema, and whether we can pull AD/audit events for GDPR eDiscovery. Also residency — EU region is a requirement for some PII.
[00:46] Omar Ruiz: Yep. On logging, Redwood produces per-token request audit logs with timestamp, model id, route, and anonymized token counts. We can export JSON or syslog to your Splunk — we commonly set up a forwarder or S3 bucket ingestion. Retention is configurable from our console; default is 90 days on hosted but Dedicated and Private can keep longer per contract.
[01:06] Dana Ortiz: Is that export real-time? We need near-real-time for incident response, ideally within a minute.
[01:12] Omar Ruiz: Typical syslog or Kinesis-forwarded streams are sub-minute; with Dedicated we can do native TCP syslog to your collector. For hosted we use TLS-encrypted pushes to your S3 or your Kinesis stream. Sometimes the docs show it as K V cache — sorry, I mean KV cache — that's unrelated.
[01:27] (laughs)
[01:30] Priya Anand: On encryption — you mentioned KMS. We need to know if keys are customer-managed and if there's HSM-backed key material.
[01:37] Maria Chen: Short answer: yes for Private deployments, and yes for Dedicated with an enterprise key management add-on. We support customer-managed keys via external KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and also HSM-backed keys via Cloud HSM or customer HSM for on-prem installs. For hosted by default keys are Redwood-managed but we can negotiate CMEK for the enterprise plan.
[01:59] Kyle Mercer: Can you provide a diagram of the key lifecycle and where plaintext ever exists?
[02:05] Omar Ruiz: We'll send a KMS architecture diagram. In short: tokens are encrypted at rest with envelope encryption, decrypted only within our runtime memory for the duration of inference; plaintext is never written to disk. Keys are rotated per policy and access is limited by RBAC roles. Some customers opt for a private deployment where key material never leaves their VPC.
[02:23] Dana Ortiz: We need evidence for that — not just a description. An auditor will want config screenshots or a playbook.
[02:29] Maria Chen: Absolutely. We'll include sample policy screenshots, and a sanitized runbook showing key rotation and HSM attestation data where available.
[02:37] [00:02:45] (speaker overlap)
[02:45] Kyle Mercer: About identity — we use Okta SSO. We need SAML metadata, SCIM support for user provisioning, and RBAC mapping so our auditor can see how least-privilege is enforced.
[02:56] Omar Ruiz: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. Roles are mapped in our Console to granular permissions — e.g., read-only cost dashboards vs deploy privileges. For auditability we keep an 'admin actions' log with who performed what, timestamped.
[03:12] Priya Anand: Do you support SCIM deprovisioning hooks? We need automated disable within 5 minutes ideally.
[03:18] Omar Ruiz: Yes, SCIM-based deprovisioning is supported and we've seen sub-60 second deprovs in many set-ups; depends on your IdP push intervals though.
[03:27] Dana Ortiz: On the assurance spreadsheet we flagged several queries around SOC 2 control categories — CC6, CC7 equivalents. Can you map those to your SOC2 Type II report?
[03:36] Maria Chen: We will. We'll send the SOC2 Type II report and a mapping doc that points to the control sections. Note: parts of our infra are outsourced to public cloud partners; those are covered in subservice organization carve-outs in the report.
[03:48] Kyle Mercer: You also support Private deployment, right? For EU residency we might need a VPC-only, isolated control plane.
[03:55] Omar Ruiz: Yes. Redwood Private offers a customer-managed control plane in your VPC, and we can ship an on-prem package for air-gapped scenarios. We call the hosted offering simply Redwood Hosted in our docs — sometimes we say Redwood Dedicated for reserved GPU pools. Sorry if names get swapped.
[04:10] Maria Chen: For the questionnaire, we'd recommend marking the residency questions as 'Yes - see Private deployment option' and we'll flag necessary lead times.
[04:19] Priya Anand: What's the lead time for Private deploy? Four to six weeks?
[04:23] Omar Ruiz: Typical is 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals and key exchange. If you need HSM attestation or lengthy change control we build that into the schedule.
[04:34] [00:05:00]
[04:35] Dana Ortiz: On logging retention, our spec requires 7 years for certain financial logs. Can Redwood support long-tail retention?
[04:43] Maria Chen: With Dedicated/Private yes — we can negotiate storage costs or integrate with your long-term S3 bucket. For hosted it's not default but we can extend retention as a billable option. We'll include cost estimates in the spreadsheet.
[04:55] Kyle Mercer: About the SIG and CAIQ forms: some questions are very granular about segmentation, network ACLs, and host hardening. Do you have standard evidence packages for those?
[05:05] Omar Ruiz: We have a security evidence repository. For SIG/CAIQ we provide a prefilled questionnaire, supporting docs (hardening checklist, patch cadence, vulnerability scanning reports) and screenshots or sanitized logs as evidence. For host hardening we can provide CIS benchmark attestation or our patch management schedule.
[05:21] Priya Anand: Will you include the most recent vuln scan? We need within 30 days.
[05:25] Omar Ruiz: We can include the latest external vuln scan summary and a remediation tracker extract, redacted for sensitive hostnames. Full reports are sometimes restricted but we provide auditor-facing artifacts on request under NDA.
[05:38] Maria Chen: Quick question for Silverpine — what's your top acceptance criteria to sign here? Is it proof of encryption, EU residency, or something else?
[05:46] Dana Ortiz: It's a combo: SOC2 coverage, KMS/CMEK path with HSM capability, and EU data residency. If those are clear with evidence, procurement moves fast.
[05:56] Kyle Mercer: Also least-privileged RBAC and audit log integration with Splunk — that's a must.
[06:02] Omar Ruiz: Noted. We'll prioritize artifacts for those three buckets.
[06:06] [00:07:00]
[06:07] Priya Anand: A couple procurement questions — standard contract terms include data processing addendum, breach notification SLA, and indemnity. Anything outside Redwood standard we should flag?
[06:18] Maria Chen: The standard DPA supports GDPR clauses and 72-hour breach notification. For enterprise we can negotiate breach SLAs and add audit rights. We can also include customer-specific residency commitments in the SOW for Private deployments.
[06:30] Dana Ortiz: Who at Redwood handles legal? We'll need contact for the DPA redlines.
[06:34] Maria Chen: I'll loop in our legal lead, Claire Benson, on the next email. Claire handles DPA and SLA redlines.
[06:41] Kyle Mercer: On the SIG mapping, can you put answers in "Yes/No/See Evidence" and a pointer to the artifact? That helps my auditors.
[06:50] Omar Ruiz: Yes — we'll provide a spreadsheet column with direct links to the evidence zip or ticket. We'll likely provide a single consolidated evidence bundle in S3 and point each question to the file name.
[06:59] [00:09:00]
[07:00] Dana Ortiz: Are there any known single points of failure in the hosted offering from a security perspective? E.g., admin access to tenant data?
[07:09] Omar Ruiz: Multi-tenant hosted uses strict tenant isolation at the application layer; admin access is logged, gated by RBAC, and requires multi-party approval for privileged ops. For high-assurance needs customers choose Dedicated or Private.
[07:22] Priya Anand: Do you provide MFA for admin console?
[07:25] Omar Ruiz: Yes, MFA is enforced for all admin roles; we support TOTP and FIDO2 for staff, and SSO-enforced MFA for customers via Okta.
[07:34] Maria Chen: A note on evidence delivery: we'll sanitize logs to remove customer token content. We do not share raw model outputs.
[07:41] Kyle Mercer: Good. For eDiscovery and GDPR we might need to prove ability to remove a customer's data on request. How does deletion work?
[07:50] Omar Ruiz: We support data deletion APIs and have formal retention workflows. For hosted we delete tokens and request metadata after retention TTLs, and we can run on-demand erasure for customer-supplied PII with proof-of-deletion artifacts. For Private the customer controls storage.
[08:05] Dana Ortiz: What's the format for your proof-of-deletion?
[08:08] Omar Ruiz: Typically a signed deletion report listing object keys removed and checksums; for deeper audits we perform a scrub and provide a third-party attestation if required.
[08:18] [00:10:00]
[08:19] Priya Anand: Can you confirm the TLS versions supported inbound? Our policy requires TLS 1.2 minimum, prefer 1.3.
[08:25] Omar Ruiz: We support TLS 1.2 and 1.3; 1.3 is preferred and enabled by default.
[08:30] Kyle Mercer: About the SOC2 report — is that Type II and what period does it cover?
[08:34] Maria Chen: It's SOC 2 Type II covering Jan–Dec 2025. We'll attach the redacted report and a controls mapping worksheet.
[08:41] Dana Ortiz: For ISO 27001, are you certified or in scope planning?
[08:44] Maria Chen: Redwood is currently in scope planning for ISO 27001 and we have an assessment plan; we are not yet certified. We'll provide a scoping note and timeline for certification.
[08:54] Priya Anand: That could be a procurement blocker for us, but SOC2 Type II plus the Private deployment option might be acceptable. We'll confirm.
[09:02] (background noise)
[09:05] Omar Ruiz: One more technical note — model artifacts and weights are treated as software assets; customers can request a CSPM-style snapshot of runtime images for our Private deployments.
[09:16] Kyle Mercer: If we go Dedicated, can we restrict which model catalog items are allowed? For compliance we sometimes whitelist models.
[09:24] Omar Ruiz: Yes you can lock the model catalog per tenant and block external model downloads. We can document that and provide the enforcement policy.
[09:31] Maria Chen: Moving to logistics: we'll put together a mapping, attach SOC2 and the KMS diagram, and send the S3 evidence bundle link. Any other high-priority artifacts?
[09:42] Dana Ortiz: The recent pen test summary and the patch cycle would be helpful.
[09:46] Omar Ruiz: We'll include the pen test executive summary and the patch cadence schedule.
[09:51] Priya Anand: For evidence delivery, prefer an S3 pre-signed bundle to our SOC team email, not a large attachment.
[09:58] Maria Chen: Noted. We'll provision a pre-signed S3 link with access controls and TTL.
[10:03] [00:12:00]
[10:04] Kyle Mercer: Pricing question — how do you price the Dedicated/Private options; is there a minimum commitment?
[10:10] Maria Chen: Dedicated has monthly reserved capacity with a 12-month commit typical; Private is custom and usually includes a platform fee and support tier. I'll send a reference pricing sheet but final numbers come in a formal quote.
[10:22] Dana Ortiz: Okay. Timeline recap? If we get SOC2 + KMS diagram this week, procurement can start intake.
[10:29] Maria Chen: Yes, our plan: SOC2 + mapping spreadsheet by Friday (Aug 7), KMS diagram by Aug 10, evidence bundle S3 link by Aug 11, then security deep-dive week of Aug 13. Does that align?
[10:42] Priya Anand: That timeline works for procurement.
[10:45] Kyle Mercer: Works for security as well.
[10:48] [00:15:00]
[10:49] Dana Ortiz: A small question about incident response: do you publish a post-incident report template? Our auditors want a sample.
[10:58] Omar Ruiz: We have an IR playbook and a sanitized postmortem template we can share. It includes timeline, root cause, scope, and remediation steps.
[11:06] Priya Anand: Please send that too.
[11:08] Maria Chen: Will do.
[11:10] (paper shuffling)
[11:14] Dana Ortiz: Any gotchas we should be aware of when filling the SIG?
[11:18] Omar Ruiz: A common gotcha is question overlap — you'll see similar controls asked under different headings; our mapping helps avoid contradictory answers. Also some evidence is shared across questions so we'll reference the same artifact multiple times.
[11:31] Maria Chen: We'll label evidence items clearly and provide MD5 checksums in the spreadsheet.
[11:36] Priya Anand: Anything from your side you need from us?
[11:39] Dana Ortiz: Please confirm the exact residency wording — "data processed in EU only" vs "data stored in EU" — we need the more restrictive one in the contract.
[11:48] Maria Chen: We'll propose contract language for "data stored and processed in EU region" for the Private deployment and flag potential caveats for hosted.
[11:57] [00:20:00]
[11:58] Kyle Mercer: One last technical: are operator console logs separate from customer audit logs? We need to see that separation for compliance.
[12:06] Omar Ruiz: Yes, operator logs (Redwood admin) are segregated and only accessible to a small ops group; customer-level logs are available to the tenant and redact PII. We'll include a diagram showing log separation and access control lists.
[12:19] Dana Ortiz: Great. I think we have what we need for next steps.
[12:22] Maria Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll send the SOC2 and mapping by Friday and loop Claire for legal redlines. Any objections to scheduling the follow-up deep-dive on Aug 13 at 10am PT?
[12:33] Priya Anand: Works for procurement.
[12:35] Kyle Mercer: Works.
[12:37] Dana Ortiz: Works.
[12:39] Maria Chen: Perfect. Thanks all.
[12:42] (meeting ends)
[52:00]
questions: Can Redwood provide SOC2 Type II report?
Do you support customer-managed KMS and HSM integration?
What's the lead time for Private deployment (VPC/on-prem)?
Can audit logs be exported to Splunk and retained 7+ years?
